HMW-V23: Intra-Trip Job Navigation

Teleport OS Vendor — Design Hypothesis

How might we let vendors navigate between jobs on the same trip — without returning to My Jobs each time?
Root cause: A vendor with multiple jobs on the same trip (e.g., DO-001 has FM + EC + OH jobs) must navigate back to My Jobs between each one: Job Detail → ← My Jobs → click next row → Job Detail. On a 10-job dispatch morning that's 18 navigations. The job detail header already shows the trip ID, but it's plain monospace text — not a link, not a navigator. Vendors have no way to know how many jobs belong to the current trip, or whether sibling jobs need action, without exiting to the list.

Context: HaleSun Logistics handles an average of 3–5 jobs per trip. Dispatchers typically open jobs in sequence (FM first to assign a driver, then EC to check customs status, then OH to confirm hub ops). The round-trip to My Jobs is dead navigation overhead.

Option A — Trip Job Strip

Option A
A compact strip sits below the header rule and above the Status Action Bar. It shows the trip ID on the left, then one chip per job in the trip (left-to-right order, current job highlighted in blue). Each chip has a 5px status dot + job ID. Click any chip to navigate. The strip is always visible when there are 2+ jobs on the trip; hidden on single-job trips. Overflow scrolls horizontally on tablet.

Pros
• Zero extra navigation steps — strip is always present
• Status dots surface sibling urgency at a glance (amber J03 needs attention)
• Compact: 24px strip height, does not displace any content
• Horizontal scroll on 768px tablet — no columns lost
• Hidden on single-job trips — no clutter
• Uses existing vocabulary (dots, job IDs, service codes)
Cons
• On trips with 10+ jobs, strip requires horizontal scroll (rare case)
• Chips show job ID + service code only — customer/route not visible (detail is one click away)
• Requires trip context data to be available in JobDetailPage (currently fetched via useTrips — already works)

Option B — Forward / Back Navigation with Next-Job Peek

Option B
The header breadcrumb gains ← / → navigation arrows that move between jobs on the current trip in their natural order (J01 → J02 → J03). The current job position is shown as a mono fraction (2/3). Each arrow also shows a small peek label of the next/previous job (service + status). This replaces the strip with a more minimal in-header pattern.

Pros
• Very minimal footprint — lives in the header, no extra layout region
• The "1/3" fraction confirms trip scope immediately
• Peek label (J02 EC · Pending) previews the next job without navigating
• Keyboard-friendly: ← → arrows are obvious affordances
Cons
• Only exposes linear sequential access — can't jump to J03 from J01 without passing through J02
• "Order" of jobs (J01→J02→J03) may not reflect urgency (amber J03 is not reachable in one click)
• Header becomes visually dense: back link + job id + service name + trip ref + customer + nav arrows
• On 768px, the nav arrows + peek label risk wrapping or truncating
• Peek label is text-only — dispatcher must remember that "Pending" means needs attention

Option C — Sibling Jobs Panel (Bottom of Page)

Option C
A collapsible "Other jobs on this trip" section at the bottom of the detail page, after the Activity Log. Collapsed by default, showing only the count: "2 more jobs on DO-001 ▾". Expanded: a compact mini-table listing sibling jobs with status, service, and route. Click any row to navigate.

Pros
• Keeps the header clean — no structural changes above
• Shows service type + route in the sibling row (richer context than a chip)
• Natural page flow: primary job first, context at the end
• Status dots inline in collapsed header give a quick signal even when collapsed
Cons
• Requires scrolling to the bottom before you can navigate (wrong ergonomics — dispatchers usually check siblings before working the current job, not after)
• Collapsed by default hides the signal — the amber J03 "To verify" is invisible until expanded
• Adds a new UI region (collapsible accordion) — a new interaction pattern for one page
• On tablet, the page is already long. Adding a sibling table below the Activity Log pushes them further down

✓ Verdict: Option A — Trip Job Strip

Why A wins: The strip answers "what else is on this trip and what state is it in?" before the dispatcher begins work on the current job — not after. It adds one 24px horizontal band with no disruption to the existing status bar → sections → log layout. The status dots surface urgency (J03 amber = to verify) in the same visual language as the rest of the app. Option B's arrows are linear and force sequential access; Option C's panel is correctly placed in the wrong spot (bottom of page, after Activity Log).

Implementation notes:
• Add a TripJobStrip component to vendor/src/components/. Receives trip.jobs + currentJobId.
• Render between the detail-header rule and the Status Action Bar, only when trip.jobs.length > 1.
• Chip styles: current job = border: 1px solid #152CFF; background: rgba(21,44,255,0.06); color: #152CFF. Other jobs = standard ghost chip with status dot derived from getJobStatusDot() helper (already in shared/statusStyles.ts).
• Click handler: navigate(\`/jobs/\${trip.id}/\${job.id}\`).
• On trips with 8+ jobs: overflow-x: auto with the strip scrolling horizontally. Count label ("N jobs on this trip") pinned at the right end.
• Hide on single-job trips: trip.jobs.length === 1 ? null : <TripJobStrip/>.

Open questions:
1. Should the strip also show a small alert badge on chips when a sibling job has status = "To verify" (Completed + Pending verification)? Recommend: no extra badge — the amber dot is sufficient signal. Badges add visual noise.
2. Should clicking a chip that belongs to a different vendor be blocked or allowed? (Vendors only see their own jobs.) Since the jobs list is already filtered to the current vendor, all sibling chips would always belong to the same vendor — no need for any restriction.
